\[
\hat{I} = \operatorname{dering}\big(\operatorname{deblock}(I)\big),
\qquad
\operatorname{deblock}(I) = \frac{1}{n^2} \sum_s S_{-s}\, J\big(S_s I\big),
\qquad
\operatorname{dering}(I) = w\, \operatorname{bilateral}(I) + (1 - w)\, I,
\qquad
q = 50,\ T = 20
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(J\): The lossy step of JPEG for quality q
- \(S_s\): A shift of the image within the 8 x 8 grid
- \(w\): The blend weight of the zone around strong edges
- \(T\): The edge threshold of the deringing step

JPEG leaves two kinds of damage. Block edges come from rounding each 8 x 8 block on its own, and ringing comes from the rounding of the fine detail next to strong edges. The first step is the deblocking filter, Nosratinia's re-application of JPEG. J is the lossy step of JPEG with the quantization tables of quality q, and S_s shifts the image within the 8 x 8 grid. The second step is the deringing filter. w is the soft weight of the zone around strong edges, and the bilateral filter smooths the ripples there. See those two filters for the details. The deblocking step also removes some ringing, so the deringing step has less to do.
